records.note: Seasonal mood change in people with bipolar disorder is a general clinical pattern, not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or practice-adoption outcome. Present-tense description ('Fall is here. And with it...') with no observable event, series or threshold.

Legacy claim about a colleague's place in a future history of psychiatry. Reputation is not one of the five areas; 'when the history ... is written' names no event, source or date. Also presupposes that psychiatric illness is healed.

Scientific inference ('it should be possible to stimulate ... to treat PTSD') with no named trial, sponsor, endpoint or benchmark. 'Treat PTSD' cannot be written as a resolvable event without inventing the program and the endpoint; no date words.

'Wildly popular medicine' is a slogan with no series, threshold or countable set, conditional on 'if this approach works', which is itself unwritten. The approach is also in use at the author's own clinics (Acacia, Fermata), but the primary failure is that no event can be written.

Block quote from Acacia's team (the author's own organization) describing what the Siddiqi study 'provides': a blueprint for TMS targeting. Descriptive of a published study; no future state, event or date is asserted.

'More publications will be forthcoming' from the PTSD-target work at Acacia Clinics and Fermata, both the author's organizations (clinician and trial site; co-founder). Publications of the forecaster's own organizations are commitments, not forecasts.
'Other systems need to catch up' is normative and 'science is not the rate-limiting step' names no system, event, series or threshold. No observable outcome can be written; no date words.
Promise of further coverage in the author's own newsletter ('stay tuned'). Own organization decides.
Expectation about the emotional reactions of party attendees after the Combs indictment. Not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or practice-adoption outcome; no measurable event.
A federal criminal case against Sean Combs is not in any of the five areas. The sentence is also a near-truism about legal process and the author explicitly declines to predict the outcome.
Expectation about third parties' future feelings of regret. Outside the five areas; no observable event.
Hedged expectation that victims' resolve will waver outside law-enforcement settings. Psychological state of unnamed people; outside the five areas and not measurable.

'So many other options are coming' is a quantifier with no countable set and no benchmark (which treatments, which milestone: trial start, readout, clearance). 'Coming' is not a deadline. The GammaCore Breakthrough status is stated as a present fact, not forecast.

'The robots would be better diagnosticians than I could ever be someday': a comparative with no benchmark, no named system, task or series, and 'someday' is not a deadline. Framed as a belief held since 2013.

'More [publications] are coming' on TDScreen, the author's own project with Videra Health (strategic advisor; TDscreen is a listed alias) and iRxReminder (Chief Medical Officer 2024). Publications of the forecaster's own organizations are commitments.
Scheduling of a guest on the author's own newsletter this weekend. Own organization decides.

Structural claim about incentives: quarterly profit 'has to go up to keep Wall Street happy'. 'Has to' states what the market demands, not the author's expectation that UnitedHealth Group's profit rises each quarter; no series, quarter or threshold is named. No lexicon phrase.

'New and more creative names' for payment-control mechanisms names no observable event, policy document or series; the author says the need 'has now been solved' by pre-payment review, so the forward reading is a general expectation with nothing resolvable. 'Need to' is also partly normative.

Denial that HIV is stopped globally. 'Stop HIV ... globally' has no series, threshold (incidence, coverage) or date; the payer or program that would decide is not named. No event can be written without inventing the metric.

Gilead's low-income-country access commitment for lenacapavir was public on the statement date (2024-10-06): the sponsor had announced an access plan with the PURPOSE 1 results and, on 2 October 2024, royalty-free voluntary licences to generic makers for 120 high-incidence, resource-limited countries. The finder flags the line as a restatement of announced commitments. Tone (sarcasm) is not read; on the words, the outcome was already determined by the sponsor.

Labelled 'My prediction', but 'everyone who needs it' and 'with alacrity' give no countable set, coverage threshold, series or date, and 'it' (Gilead, the discount program or the system) is not identified. No event can be written without inventing the metric.
The two closing sentences are already captured verbatim inside owen-1259 (same post, same statement); the first row stands. The line also restates owen-1257.
Present-tense account of the author's own prescribing ('this is a go-to treatment option') and his opinion of existing data ('promising'). No future state asserted for GammaCore nVNS.
Promise of a future column on smart glasses in the author's own newsletter. Own organization decides.

Predicted effects of a proposed national medical licence ('increase labor mobility', 'reduce drivers of cost', 'improve the ability') are comparatives with no benchmark or series, conditional on a policy that does not exist and is not itself forecast. Advocacy with no resolvable event.

Marked parody: a 'Ring-of-Power Notification' from 'Mordor Partners, Inc.' mimicking the Change Healthcare breach letter. The aside that breaches 'seem to happen regularly' is a jab inside the satire, with no entity, series or threshold.

A proposal ('I propose a Hallmark Card') framed as a business opportunity. Statement of preference and assessment; no future state (a product launch, a sales figure) is asserted for any named company.
'Destigmatizing' has no series, threshold or deciding body, and the claim is conditional on proposed cards that do not exist. Stigma reduction is also outside the five areas.

event.asset: Optum / UnitedHealthcare pre-payment review of mental health claims (parity compliance)
event.entity: US federal or state courts; US Department of Labor (EBSA), state attorneys general or state insurance regulators (deciding bodies); UnitedHealthcare, United Behavioral Health and Optum (respondents)
event.title: Parity litigation or enforcement over UnitedHealthcare/Optum pre-payment review of mental health claims
event.proposition: A lawsuit or a regulator enforcement action alleging that UnitedHealthcare, United Behavioral Health or Optum's pre-payment review of mental health claims violates mental health parity law is filed.
event.criterion: TRUE on the docket date of the first complaint filed in a US federal or state court, or the announcement date of the first enforcement action by the US Department of Labor, a state attorney general or a state insurance regulator, that names UnitedHealthcare, United Behavioral Health or Optum as defendant or respondent and alleges that pre-payment review (post-service, pre-payment claim review) of mental health or substance use disorder claims violates the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act or a state mental health parity law. A complaint or action about prior authorization or another utilization-review practice that does not name pre-payment review does not count. A filed complaint counts; no verdict, order or settlement is needed. Resolved on court docket records (CourtListener); regulator press releases are a secondary source.

resolution_source.name: CourtListener (RECAP federal and state dockets); DOL/EBSA and New York Attorney General press releases as secondary

readings: 'Yet more litigation' is read as a new parity complaint or enforcement action over the pre-payment review policy the post describes, after the 2021 DOL / New York AG settlement the author quotes. A private (individual or class) complaint or a public enforcement action both count.
court_outcome is the closest template for a litigation claim; the event resolves on initiation (docket date of the complaint or announcement of the enforcement action), not on a later ruling.

records.phrase: it seems it might be the basis for yet more litigation
records.stage_note: At the statement date (2024-10-14), per the post: the 2021 Department of Labor / New York Attorney General settlement with United Behavioral Health and UnitedHealthcare ($13.6 million to beneficiaries, $2,084,249 in penalties) was public, and Optum's pre-payment review policy was in force; the author names no complaint or enforcement action over pre-payment review. No base-rate class covers litigation filings, so b is null.
records.note: Hedged forecast phrased with a question mark; 'might' is the strongest phrase in the claim sentence and sets bin C. The event is written on the policy (pre-payment review), not on the corporate name, and resolves on the filing of litigation or an enforcement action, as with earlier court_outcome enforcement items. No horizon words: undated panel, 24-month window from 2024-10-14. Not affiliated: the author holds no disclosed role in UnitedHealthcare, Optum, the Department of Labor or a state regulator; Radial is a provider and is not named in the event. A coder who reads the question mark as pure speculation would reject VAGUE.

Denial that UnitedHealthcare gives 'more transparency': a comparative with no benchmark. The author does not say which disclosure would count (WARN notices, a layoff count, an offshore headcount), so no event can be written without inventing it; no date words.
Promise of the next installment of the author's own MBT visual guide in his newsletter. Own organization decides.
Sign-off promising the next newsletter installment tomorrow. Own organization decides; a different post from owen-1279, so not DUPLICATE.
